title: Wrapper honours agentProvider at spawn; pause bookkeeping is per-provider
description:
SPIDR grandchild D of task-8e793ae3c63f41189bcc05f6d7c15605 (architect-2e480458, 2026-09-05). dependsOn grandchild C (the store must exist to honour).

MEASURED INVARIANT: agent-provider-pause.ts:36 and agent-wrapper.ts:323-325 state ONE MOE_AGENT_COMMAND PER WRAPPER PROCESS. agent-spawner.ts:50 resolves `options.command ?? process.env["MOE_AGENT_COMMAND"] ?? "claude"` ONCE at spawnRuntime construction; agent-wrapper-main.ts:291 passes that one provider into createProviderPauseGate. The pause LEDGER is already keyed by (projectId, provider) — readProviderPause(store, projectId, provider, …). Option (a) is the smallest production-reachable slice that satisfies argv[0] changing with the setting inside one wrapper; option (b) would require two wrapper processes the launcher does not start.

WHAT THIS ROW OWNS: per-spawn resolution (new module), spawner uses it inside attemptSpawn (codexSeat becomes per-spawn), wrapper staffing skips only the paused provider's steps, pause gate records/reads per the seat's provider, wrapper-main stops freezing one provider at process start.

NOT IN SCOPE: /sessions/read disclosure (grandchild E), UI, command kind roster.

VERIFY: `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test`.
definitionOfDone: A test asserts argv[0] is `codex` when the durable setting says codex and `claude` when it says claude, with MOE_AGENT_COMMAND unset. The assertion is against the spawned argv, not an internal field. The codex-only env allowlist is applied for a codex spawn.
With MOE_AGENT_COMMAND set, the spawn uses it REGARDLESS of the setting. Assert argv[0] matches the env value.

Pause is per-provider: a live pause for claude does not prevent staffing a codex goal (and the reverse). A test covers a pause under this model. The comment at agent-wrapper.ts:323-325 no longer claims one MOE_AGENT_COMMAND per wrapper process.
Gates quoted with `Test Files N passed`: `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test`, `pnpm typecheck`.
taskRails: INVARIANT DECISION, BINDING: option (a) PER-SPAWN RESOLUTION. The wrapper resolves the provider PER SPAWN (env > goal override > project setting > claude). Pause bookkeeping is per-provider, not per-wrapper. Do not take option (b) (one provider per process, two wrappers). Record this in the step note; a later worker must not re-decide it.

EXTRACT, DO NOT GROW. agent-spawner.ts is 438 lines and agent-wrapper-main.ts is 482 (both over the 400 cap). New agent-provider-resolve.ts owns precedence. Update the comment at agent-wrapper.ts:323-325 that currently states one MOE_AGENT_COMMAND per process.
Assert spawned argv[0], not an internal field. Codex-only env allowlist (agent-spawn-environment.ts:22-24) applies when the resolved command is a codex seat.
MOE_AGENT_COMMAND still wins at spawn. Disclosure of that win on /sessions/read is grandchild E, not this row.
FEATURES ONLY. No UI, no MCP fence, no contract roster.

implementationPlan.description: THE RESOLVER MODULE. NEW FILE apps/daemon/src/orchestrator/agent-provider-resolve.ts (target <=250 lines) plus its .js bridge if this repo's convention requires one for a new orchestrator module - check a sibling (agent-provider-pause.js exists beside agent-provider-pause.ts) and follow it; a missing bridge kills the daemon at boot with ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND. THE SEAM, DECIDED HERE SO THE WORKER DOES NOT RE-DERIVE IT: the WRAPPER resolves the provider and puts the resolved command on the request; the SPAWNER consumes it. Reasoning, which belongs in the step note: the spawner has no store handle and no project context, while `staff()` in agent-wrapper.ts already holds `config.projectId` and the step - so resolution at the wrapper is the only place with the facts, and it keeps precedence in ONE module rather than split across two. Export `resolveAgentProvider(input)` implementing the precedence the rail binds, IN THIS ORDER: (1) `process.env["MOE_AGENT_COMMAND"]` if set - it still wins at spawn, DoD-2; (2) the per-GOAL override from the store; (3) the per-PROJECT setting; (4) the literal "claude". Take the store as an injected LAZY FACT FUNCTION, not a store handle - `(projectId, goalRef) => string | null` - matching the convention this codebase already documents three times in PlanningOfferInput ("A FACT rather than a store handle... stays pure"). That keeps this module unit-testable with no sqlite and lets wrapper-main own the composition. ALSO EXPORT the codex predicate currently inlined at agent-spawner.ts:76 (`/(?:^|[\\/])codex(?:\.[a-z]+)?$/iu`) as a named function, so the spawner imports one definition rather than keeping a second copy. Its test (agent-provider-resolve.test.ts, also new) asserts each precedence rung IN ISOLATION and, critically, each rung WINNING OVER THE ONE BELOW IT - a test that only checks "env wins" and "default is claude" leaves the middle two rungs unproven and is exactly the sweep that passes while the goal override never fires.

- `resolveAgentProvider(input: {envCommand?, goalRef?, settingFor?}): string` — precedence env > goal override > project setting > "claude". Always returns a non-empty string.
- `isCodexCommand(command): boolean` — the ONE definition of the codex predicate, regex `/(?:^|[\\/])codex(?:\.[a-z]+)?$/iu` lifted verbatim from agent-spawner.ts:76. Step 3 makes the spawner import it instead of keeping a second copy.
- `pauseProviderOf(command): "claude"|"codex"` — maps a resolved COMMAND to the pause ledger's provider key via the existing `providerFor()` (moe-up-credentials.ts:143), unknown -> "claude". Added here (not planned) so step 4 can make the per-step pause decision a one-liner: agent-wrapper.ts has only 2 lines of headroom under the 400 cap, so nothing sizeable may land there.

TWO DESIGN POINTS THE PLAN DID NOT SETTLE, decided and recorded:
1. THE INJECTED FACT IS AN EXACT-SCOPE LOOKUP, `(goalId) => string | null`, NOT the store's collapsing port. Measured reason: `readAgentProvider` (agent-provider-store.ts:76-80) ALREADY does `values.get(goalId) ?? values.get("") ?? "claude"` internally, so a collapsing fact would make rungs 2 and 3 indistinguishable — the goal-override arm would pass while the override never fired. The test's `facts()` helper is deliberately exact-scope and says so in a comment.
2. RUNG 3 IS LOAD-BEARING IN PRODUCTION, not defensive padding: rung 2 is consulted ONLY when `goalRef` is a non-empty string, so every `node.deliver` seat (whose aggregateId is a nodeRef, never a goal) takes rung 3 directly. That is the plan's stated limit made structural rather than commented.
Also: the fact is read through a try/catch that answers "no setting" — a store refusal (AGENT_PROVIDER_STORE_UNREADABLE) must not wedge staffing. Blank/whitespace envCommand and blank goalRef both read as UNSET rather than as values.

Imported the existing one instead; there is now exactly one "claude" literal for this concept in the module.

implementationPlan.note:
PAUSE PER PROVIDER — landed. Typecheck EXIT 0; orchestrator suite `Test Files  46 passed (46)` / `Tests  671 passed | 1 skipped (672)`.

(1) agent-provider-pause.ts (186 -> 205). The gate no longer serves ONE frozen provider.
- `paused(nowMs, provider?)` and `exitObserver(sessionId, workItemId, refund, provider?)` both take the SEAT's provider. Both new parameters are OPTIONAL and fall back to `config.provider` via one `seatOf()` helper, so every existing 3-arg/1-arg call site keeps today's behaviour byte for byte — that is why all pre-existing pause tests stayed green without edits.
- The provider is threaded all the way down, not just into the read: `livePause`, `resetFor`, `recordExit`, `park` and `observe` each take it, and `classifySeatExit({provider})` now gets the SEAT's provider. Threading only `paused` would have left a codex seat's limit exit recorded and parked under "claude" — a silent cross-provider park, which is exactly the bug this row retires.
- The ledger needed NO change: `readProviderPause(store, projectId, provider, iso)` and `recordProviderPause`/`recordSeatExit` were already keyed by (projectId, provider). Re-verified at the tree; that is the measured reason invariant option (a) is the small slice.
- THE RETIRED DOCBLOCK at :36 is rewritten. It no longer says "one MOE_AGENT_COMMAND per wrapper process"; it now states that the wrapper serves many providers, that each seat's command is resolved per spawn, that the pause is per (project, provider), and that `config.provider` is only a fallback for a caller that resolved none.

(2) agent-wrapper.ts (398 -> 399). The pass-level short-circuit at :334-343 is DELETED, comment and all — that was the second copy of the retired invariant (DoD-3).
- The decision is now PER STEP inside the loop: `decideSeatProvider({aggregateId, kind, nowMs, pauseGate, settingFor})` returns `{command, pause}` from ONE resolution, so the command the pause was checked against is provably the command the seat is spawned with. A live claude pause `continue`s past claude steps while a codex goal still staffs.
- A step skipped for a pause is charged NO attempt: it `continue`s before `attempts.set(...)`, so the existing GATE_REFUSALS accounting needed no edit.
- `staff(step, command)` puts `provider: command` on the request AND passes `pauseProviderOf(command)` to `exitObserver`, so the seat's exit is classified/recorded/parked under its own provider.

REPORTING SHAPE — THE DELIBERATE CHOICE THE PLAN ASKED FOR, recorded verbatim:
A pass reports `surfaceOutcome: PROVIDER_PAUSED` and carries `paused` ONLY when a live pause is why the pass staffed NOTHING (`stalled !== null && spawned.length === 0`). comments.content:
THE ROW'S RAIL BINDS THE INVARIANT BUT NOT THE SEAM — and the seam is where the real work is. architect-b63fabf3, 2026-09-05, HEAD f3b94eaa. Plan approved: 6 steps, 8 files (2 new).

## The structural gap the description does not name

Rail 2 says "spawner uses it inside attemptSpawn". Measured, the spawner **has nothing to resolve from**:

```
SpawnRequest      (agent-wrapper.ts:44-55)     credential, expiresAt, kind, mission,
                                               sessionId, workItemId, workspace
                                               -> no projectId, no goalRef
AgentSpawnerOptions (agent-spawn-contract.ts:18-43)  command?, environment?, spawn?, …
                                               -> no store handle
```

A worker following the rail's words alone reaches step 2 and finds `attemptSpawn` cannot see a project or a goal. So the plan decides the seam: **the wrapper resolves, the spawner consumes.** `staff()` (agent-wrapper.ts:295-298) already holds `config.projectId` and the step, and already threads `projectId` into all three mission builders — it is the only site with the facts. The spawner reads `request.provider ?? options.command ?? env ?? "claude"`, so `codexSeat` still becomes per-spawn inside `attemptSpawn` exactly as the rail requires.

## `SpawnRequest.provider` is OPTIONAL, and that is load-bearing

`git grep -ln 'credential:' -- apps/daemon/src/orchestrator` names **six** other files that build a SpawnRequest (agent-authority-cleanup, plus five test files). A required field drags all six in and turns an 8-file row into 14. Optional keeps them out *and* makes the no-provider path byte-identical to today — which is what the fourth arm in step 5 exists to prove.

## Why option (a) really is the small slice

The pause **ledger is already keyed by provider**: `readProviderPause(store, projectId, provider, iso)` at agent-provider-pause.ts:66. What is frozen is the **gate**, not the ledger — built once at agent-wrapper-main.ts:287-292 and consulted **once per pass** at agent-wrapper.ts:326, before the step loop. So per-provider pause = move that check into the step loop. No ledger change at all.

## Three things a worker would otherwise hit mid-flight

1. **Two files are already over the 400-line cap** — agent-spawner.ts (438) and agent-wrapper-main.ts (485) — and **agent-wrapper.ts is at 394, six lines of headroom**, while needing a SpawnRequest field, a resolver call, and a per-step pause decision. That is why the new module exists; agent-wrapper-staffing.ts (186) is the second landing site.
2. **The per-goal override cannot cover `node.deliver` seats.** Their `step.aggregateId` is a nodeRef, not a goal, and no node→goal mapping exists. The plan states the limit and forbids inventing a lookup or passing a nodeRef where a goalRef is expected (it would silently miss every override).
3. **`runPass` reports `PROVIDER_PAUSED_OUTCOME` for the whole pass.** Once one provider can be paused while another staffs, that signal becomes ambiguous — and it is the wrapper's only operator-facing output. Step 4 requires the worker choose deliberately and say which.

## Two docblocks state the retired invariant verbatim

agent-provider-pause.ts:36 ("one MOE_AGENT_COMMAND per wrapper process") and agent-wrapper.ts:323-325. DoD-3 names only the second; the plan fixes both, or the next reader re-learns a rule this row deleted.

## Global rail 13 genuinely fires here, unlike most rows

The drill paths are **mixed**: agent-provider-resolve.ts and its test are new (`??`), so `git diff` is blind to them — SHA256 against an out-of-tree backup. The six pre-existing files are tracked — empty `git diff` is their proof. The plan requires saying which proof applies to which path rather than applying one rule to all eight.

The middle precedence rungs are the silent-failure risk: a suite proving only "env wins" and "default is claude" leaves the goal override and project setting untested. Drill (ii) exists to catch an override rung that never really fired.

THE ROW'S RAIL BINDS THE INVARIANT (option (a), per-spawn resolution) BUT NOT THE SEAM, and the seam is where the real decision is. A worker following the rail's words alone ("spawner uses it inside attemptSpawn") would reach step 2 and discover the spawner has nothing to resolve FROM.

It adds `provider` to the request; the spawner reads `request.provider ?? options.command ?? env ?? "claude"`. `codexSeat` still becomes per-spawn inside `attemptSpawn`, satisfying the rail. Precedence lives in ONE new module.

MEASURED 2026-09-05 by architect-b63fabf3 at HEAD f3b94eaa on moe/work-2026-09-04.

1. THE GAP THE ROW DOES NOT NAME. `SpawnRequest` at agent-wrapper.ts:44-55 = {credential, expiresAt, kind, mission, sessionId, workItemId, workspace}. No projectId, no goalRef. `AgentSpawnerOptions` at agent-spawn-contract.ts:18-43 = {command?, environment?, killProcessGroup?, killGraceMs?, log?, onFatalContainment?, output?, spawn?, timeoutMs?, platform?}. No store. This is why the seam had to be decided at plan time.

2. TODAY'S RESOLUTION, all module-scope and frozen at construction: agent-spawner.ts:50 `const command = options.command ?? process.env["MOE_AGENT_COMMAND"] ?? "claude"`; :76 `const codexSeat = /(?:^|[\\/])codex(?:\.[a-z]+)?$/iu.test(command)`. `codexSeat` is read at THREE sites inside attemptSpawn - :85 (the codex argv: exec/--ignore-user-config/--skip-git-repo-check/--ephemeral/--sandbox), :120 (only the claude seat writes the on-disk MCP config), :153 (the codex seat carries CODEX_BEARER_VARIABLE in the child env). Moving `command` inside attemptSpawn moves all three with no change to their logic.

3. THE REQUEST IS BUILT AT agent-wrapper.ts:295-298 inside `staff()`, which already reads `config.projectId` for every mission builder (:276, :286, :290) and holds `step.aggregateId`. For COMPILER steps aggregateId IS the goal (config.compilerGateRef?.(step.aggregateId) at :285); for a node.deliver step `brief !== null` and aggregateId is the nodeRef - so there is no goal to key an override on for node seats.

4. THE PAUSE IS ALREADY LEDGER-KEYED BY PROVIDER, which is the measured reason option (a) is the small slice: `readProviderPause(store, projectId, provider, iso)` at agent-provider-pause.ts:66. What is frozen is the GATE, not the ledger - agent-wrapper-main.ts:287-292 constructs it once with `provider: providerFor(process.env["MOE_AGENT_COMMAND"] ?? "claude")?.leaf ?? "claude"`, and agent-wrapper.ts:326 consults it ONCE PER PASS before the step loop. Two docblocks state the retired invariant verbatim and must be rewritten: agent-provider-pause.ts:36 and agent-wrapper.ts:323-325.

5. `runPass` returns `{active, paused, spawned, surfaceOutcome: PROVIDER_PAUSED_OUTCOME}` when paused (agent-wrapper.ts:327-332). Per-provider pause makes "the pass is paused" ambiguous - a deliberate choice, not a detail, since this is the wrapper's only operator-facing signal.

6. FILE CAPS, the binding constraint: agent-spawner.ts 438 (OVER 400 at merge-base), agent-wrapper-main.ts 485 (OVER), agent-wrapper.ts 394 (SIX lines of headroom), agent-provider-pause.ts 186, agent-spawn-contract.ts 229, agent-wrapper-staffing.ts 186 (room to absorb logic). Test files: agent-spawner.test.ts 1090, agent-provider-pause.test.ts 687 - test files are exempt from the production cap.

7. THE ARGV ASSERTION PRECEDENT ALREADY EXISTS: agent-spawner.test.ts:278 `expect(child.file).toBe("codex")`. And the WIN32 CAVEAT is documented at :101 and :181-182 - on Windows the argv collapses into one shell line and `child.args` is empty, so args-shaped assertions need a platform guard.

8. THE `.js` BRIDGE CONVENTION HOLDS in this directory: agent-provider-pause.js sits beside agent-provider-pause.ts. A new orchestrator module without its bridge kills the daemon at boot with ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND.
